newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Interview-Lion gains Aust. market share.
newsitem.headline: Interview-Lion gains Aust. market share.

text.p: Lion Nathan Chief Executive Douglas Myers said on Monday the brewer had gained market share in Australia over the last two months and that its position in New Zealand had stabilised.
Myers said in an interview Lion's market share in New Zealand was 54.4 percent, unchanged from a year ago, while that of its competitor, DB Group Ltd had risen slightly.
In the all important Australian market, where 70 percent of its assets are tied up, Lion Nathan last year reported a drop in market share to 42 percent from 43.4 percent.
"Our brands are in good shape. Our structure has now settled down and we've been into it for four or five months. We are profitable across the board," Myers told Reuters.
In Australia, Lion had market share leadership in three of the five states. "In the last couple of months it's actually become a bit stronger (in Australia).
"The position in Australia is that it is improving and in New Zealand we are stable," Myers said. He declined to elaborate with a precise market share breakdown .
Lion Nathan's main competitor, Fosters Brewing Group's Carlton United Breweries (CUB), said in February it had achieved market share of 55 percent.
Lion is to report its first half result late this month.
Analysts, citing declining sales, expect the company to fall short of the NZ$91.2 million profit achieved in the six months to February, 1996.
